title: Affine power sections at points belonging to a unique component
statement: Let X be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and C_a → X (a in Fin r) distinct reduced closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ranges irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] covering X. Let L be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] whose tensor pullback to each C_a [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. For any x in X lying on exactly one C_a there are n>0, s in Gamma(X,L^n), and an affine open U containing x equal to the nonvanishing locus of s. This makes no assertion at points belonging to two components.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof final paragraph (steps 5-7 of lem-sc-reduced-dim-le-one-ample), and Remark 09NW; Properties 01Q3 and 01PV

proof.text: Let a be the unique component containing x. The finite union of the other components is closed. Give it its reduced induced structure Z, let I be its vanishing ideal and I_a its image on C_a. The lift of x is outside V(I_a). Compactness of C_a follows from its closed immersion into compact X.

Apply the ample ideal section theorem to the ample restriction of L and I_a at the lift of x. Obtain t1 in a positive tensor power coming from the ideal, nonvanishing at x. The ample criterion also yields a positive power section t2 with affine locus through x. Multiply these sections: the degree is positive, the product still comes from I_a, and its locus is the intersection of the two loci. The affine-cap-section-open theorem makes this intersection affine inside the affine locus of t2.

Use the canonical tensor-power pullback isomorphisms and the conductor section theorem to extend the product to a global section of L^n, zero on Z. Its locus is the image of the affine component locus. On X minus Z, C_a → X is a surjective closed immersion of reduced schemes, hence an isomorphism: its ideal is zero, since all its local sections vanish at every point in this reduced open. Thus the image is an affine open of X containing x. If r=1, Z is empty and I=O_X. If r=0 the unique-component hypothesis is impossible.
